cards.explanation: The first thing David asks for is that God save him by His name. It's the very first thing out of his mouth: "Save me, O God, by Your name, and vindicate me by Your might!" (Psalm 54:1) He doesn't open with a plan or a complaint, friends. He goes straight to God and asks for rescue. I think that tells you where he knew help would come from.

David is pleading because ruthless men are out to take his life. He says, "For strangers rise up against me, and ruthless men seek my life—men with no regard for God." (Psalm 54:3) Those words are why he's begging God to hear him. When somebody is after your life, you don't pray a casual little prayer, friends.

The answer is False. After the Selah, David says, "Surely God is my helper; the Lord is the sustainer of my soul." (Psalm 54:4) No abandonment anywhere, just a man declaring that God helps him and sustains him. That's a big shift in the middle of a scary song.
The answer is False. David says of God, "He will reward my enemies with evil." (Psalm 54:5) He doesn't say "I will." He puts it in God's hands, which, honestly, is a better spot for it than mine.

David promises to sacrifice to the LORD freely. He says, "Freely I will sacrifice to You…" (Psalm 54:6) That word freely stands out to me, friends. I think he means it as a gift he's glad to give, not something he's dragged into.

The answer is True. David says, "I will praise Your name, O LORD, for it is good." (Psalm 54:6) He gives the reason right in the promise: the name is good. So he's got a sacrifice and some praise lined up, friends.

David says God has delivered him from every trouble. That's the closing reason in his song: "For He has delivered me from every trouble…" (Psalm 54:7) Every trouble, friends, not just the easy ones. That's a lot of praise material.
The answer is False. David says, "…my eyes have looked in triumph on my foes." (Psalm 54:7) The man who started the song begging for rescue ends it looking in triumph. Quite the change, friends.
